ideal: Alert on Meta’s 6.98% drop vs the index (1.18% down) with the same-day 10-Q flagged, plus Berkshire’s unusual 1.48% up day vs a down index, plus the Tesla 10-Q, all with correct signs, no invention, and links on filings.

verdicts.note: Gets all four events: Meta's big drop vs the index, Berkshire's unusual up day, and both 10-Qs with plain-word labels and links. Numbers match the report, signs are written correctly, and it correctly declines to blame the 10-Q for the drop (“no filing explains it yet”) while still surfacing the filing. Within 5 lines, no advice.
verdicts.answer:
Meta Platforms fell 6.98% (S&P 500 fell 1.18%); no filing explains it yet  
Berkshire Hathaway rose 1.48% while the S&P 500 fell 1.18% — no filing explains it yet  
Meta Platforms 10-Q quarterly report: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026066773/meta-20260930.htm  
Tesla 10-Q quarterly report: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026066775/tsla-20260930.htm

verdicts.note: Only covers Meta. Misses Berkshire's flagged move and Tesla's 10-Q, gives no link for the Meta 10-Q, and crams move and filing into one confusing line where “10-Q filed” sits right next to “no filing explains it yet.” The headline item is handled, but thinly.
verdicts.answer: Meta Platforms fell 6.98% while S&P 500 fell 1.18%. 10-Q filed. no filing explains it yet.

verdicts.note: Covers all four events, but “earnings-lagging filing” is invented — the evidence never ties the 10-Q to the drop or to earnings, and the rule says to say “no filing explains it yet” instead. “Current-quarter” is also an unsupported descriptor for the Tesla 10-Q. The numbers themselves are right.
verdicts.answer:
Meta fell 6.98% vs S&P 500 fell 1.18% — earnings‑lagging filing: 10‑Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026066773/meta-20260930.htm
Berkshire rose 1.48% vs S&P 500 fell 1.18% — no material filing
Tesla filed current‑quarter 10‑Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828026066775/tsla-20260930.htm
